title: ADULA Angle Grinder
subtitle: An 18V cordless angle grinder with a double-layer protective guard
context: School project at SIVA DeTao School of Design, Shanghai
summary: ADULA is an 18V lithium cordless angle grinder with a double-layer protective guard and an adjustable counter-handle, designed with Tao Ye between 2022 and 2023. It is an early, conceptual project from a stage when I was focused squarely on a clear problem and a mechanical answer. We tried to make it as complete as we could, inside and out, though it has not been validated in real use.

sections.heading: What I saw in research
sections.body:
From my research into how angle grinders are handled, I saw a wide range of practices, and in certain settings uses that went against safety rules. Many people without proper training were taking the same tool and using it both to grind and to cut.

That led me to ask whether one tool could be designed to cover both jobs more safely. On the guard side, we centred the concept on a double-layer protective cover conceived to recognise pressure, temperature and holding position, closing automatically before danger strikes so a blade cannot fly out.

sections.heading: Changing angle to switch tasks
sections.body:
To handle cutting, grinding and disc changes cleanly, we built the body around an adjustable counter-handle that rotates into different grip positions and speeds up blade swaps when moving from cutting to sanding. We sketched curved body shapes around motor placement and tested two-handed holds on yellow modelling foam across all three tasks.

Looking back, letting the tool be gripped at different angles to switch between cutting and grinding still feels like a creative direction to me.

sections.heading: Pushing the internals and model
sections.body:
Even as an early concept, we tried to make the structure as complete as we could, inside as well as out. The exploded head lays out the outer and inner protective covers, magnetic stripe, switch, top green screen, motor, pinion and large bevel gear alongside four discs, including grinding wheels and a toothed saw blade. We finished the body in Ferrari red and black under the name ADULA, which carries the meaning of cutting.

After iterating proportions in yellow foam, we carved a physical model in red high-density foam, painted the main body and separate side handle red and black with 18V MAX graphics, and assembled them on the bench. Pushing the internals and physical model that far is what I still appreciate about the work, alongside its clear limit. Neither the sensing guard nor the dual-mode layout has been properly validated in actual use, and both would need real testing before going further.
